# Proposal

`sales.obj.core.proposal` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> The document that states scope, price and terms. Its real audience is the room we are not in — the committee meeting, the finance review, the forward to a boss who has never heard of us — which is the single most useful thing to know about it. A proposal is therefore judged on whether it survives being forwarded without us there to explain it, not on whether it read well in the meeting where we walked through it. That discriminator separates a Proposal from a Pricing object: pricing is what a thing costs, a proposal is an argument that ends in a number and must make that argument alone.


Also called: `Quote`, `Offer`, `Commercial Proposal`, `SOW Draft`

## Constraints

- **`pr.cannot_send_without_approver`** Cannot send before a Decision Maker is identified.
- **`pr.cannot_price_below_floor`** discount_bp cannot exceed the approved discount floorwithout named internal approval.
- **`pr.one_live_version_only`** Only one non-superseded version may exist per deal.
- **`pr.terms_bind_the_contract`** Anything conceded in a proposal is conceded in the contract.There is no walking a term back at paper stage without cost.
- **`pr.expiry_must_be_real`** valid_until must be a date we will act on. _(soft)_


## Business rules

- **`pr.no_send_without_identified_approver`** A proposal must not be sent before a Decision Maker is identified. Sending priced paper to a recommender hands the buyer a document to negotiate against and gives us no one to close.
- **`pr.no_send_without_budget_range`** A priced proposal requires at least a budget range on the deal. Pricing blind is the most expensive guess in the cycle and it is made in writing.
- **`pr.must_stand_alone`** A proposal with requires_narration = true must not be the sole artefact sent. Attach the one-page summary or book the readout — the committee will not ask us to explain it, they will simply not choose us.
- **`pr.one_live_version`** Exactly one version may be live at a time. Superseding must mark the prior version superseded in the same pass, or the buyer negotiates against whichever version favours them.
- **`pr.discount_requires_reciprocity`** A change to discount_bp requires a recorded ask in return — term length, timing, references, scope. A concession given for nothing teaches the buyer that the next one is also free.
- **`pr.expiry_is_a_commitment`** If valid_until is set it must be enforced or explicitly renegotiated. A silently extended expiry destroys the credibility of every future deadline we set with this account.

## Actions

- **Draft the proposal** (human) —
- **Test it without narration** (agent) — Read it as a strangerwould. If the problem, the number and the reason for now are not all findable in two minutes, it will lose the meeting we are not in.
- **Send the proposal** (human) —
- **Brief the recipient on how to present it internally** (human) — The highest-leverage and least-used action on this object. The champion presents our proposal without us; arming them beats improving the document.
- **Chase a silent proposal** (human) —
- **Reshape scope to the funded number** (human) — Change what is bought, not what it costs. Discounting to fit a budget resets the renewal baseline permanently.
- **Issue a revised version** (human) — Supersede the prior versionexplicitly in the same pass.
- **Withdraw the proposal** (human) — Rare and occasionally correct.An offer left open indefinitely is not an offer.

## Metrics

- **proposal_to_close_rate** (percent) — Share of sent proposals that reach signature.
- **time_to_first_response** (hours) — Measured against the buyer's own baselinecadence, not the calendar.
- **revision_count_per_win** (count) — Revisions on won deals versus lost. Separateshealthy iteration from an unagreed scope.
- **committee_reach_rate** (percent) — Share of proposals confirmed seen beyondthe primary recipient. Unmeasurable today; the reason document telemetry is the top ask.
- **average_discount_bp** (bp) — Concession against list, by segment. The numberthat predicts next year's renewal margin.
- **silent_proposal_share** (percent) — Sent proposals with no reply beyond threecadence multiples.


## Examples

- **Twelve-slide deck with pricing on slide eleven** — Reads perfectly with a rep narratingand is unintelligible forwarded. The classic misclassification — logged as a strong proposal because the meeting went well.
- **Two-page summary plus a detailed appendix** — The shape that survives a forward. Thesummary is for the committee, the appendix is for the one person who will actually check the numbers.
- **Priced above budget, price objection follows** — A good state read as a bad one. Theystill want it and have told us the size of the gap for free.
- **Fourth revision in three weeks** — Looks like momentum in the activity log. Scope wasnever agreed and every version resets the buyer's anchor lower.
- **Sent, opened once, never forwarded** — Indistinguishable today from sent-and-under-review.Opposite responses required: one needs a better document, the other needs a different reader.

> Six of eleven patterns are executable; five are blocked. The blocked set has a clear shape — the pipeline can see that a proposal LEFT and almost nothing about what happened to it afterwards. The single highest-value gap is document telemetry (derived.document_unique_viewers plus a proposal_viewed observation): it converts reaches_committee, the most predictive field on this object, from a rep's guess into a fact, and unknown viewers would surface a buying committee weeks before any introduction observation fires. Second is proposal_revised — today a fourth revision and a first issue emit the identical proposal_sent observation, so stalling is indistinguishable from progress.
